content.title: Who is Boozer twins' mom? Meet Duke supermom CeCe Boozer and her viral support of the Blue Devils
content.text: Lorrayne Mavromatis, a former employee at the social media company founded by YouTube star Jimmy Donaldson, known online as MrBeast, has filed a federal lawsuit alleging years of sexual harassment, gender discrimination and retaliation by senior leadership, including Donaldson himself. Newsweek has reviewed a Slack message exchange around one allegation in the suit, which does not name MrBeast, the first YouTube creator to become a billionaire, as a defendant. The lawsuit, filed on Wednesday in North Carolina, is being supported by the Time’s Up Legal Defense Fund, which is providing media assistance in the case. The suit alleged that Mavromatis was excluded from all-male meetings because she was uncomfortable with conversations that were taking place, that harassment of female employees was normalized and that she was ultimately fired after raising these concerns and taking maternity leave. Newsweek obtained a screenshot of a Slack conversation from the day Mavromatis gave birth between her and a colleague. In the messages, a coworker, identified as Frank, tells her that they should connect to “discuss the ideas” she had. Mavromatis tells Frank that she’ll need to “cancel and postpone” because she’s in labor at the hospital. “Oh s— BUT OF COURSE hehe,” Frank responds. “Amazing! You shouldn’t even be checking slack now LOL. Sending a big hug and lots of success! Enjoy the most amazing experience of your life!” Tania Stewart, an attorney for Mavromatis, told Newsweek that the Slack message with Frank was related to “another issue” and not the meeting that Mavromatis participated in that day. Stewart added that as a co-worker and not her boss, Frank didn’t have the authority to “relieve her of any obligation to participate in the meeting.” “She was expected in the meeting and knew that if she did not join, there would be repercussions as it was ingrained in all employees to never say no and she was reminded that those that did were no longer working at MrBeast,” Stewart said. Mavromatis told Vulture that when she told her boss she was in labor and he asked whether she’d still join a scheduled team meeting. “I was so fearful of losing my job,” she told the outlet. “I knew that I didn’t want to give them any excuse for letting me go.” Mavromatis alleged in the lawsuit that there was a pattern of retaliation against employees who spoke up about workplace issues, particularly women who raised concerns related to harassment or discrimination. According to the complaint, those concerns were met with resistance rather than corrective action. She said her newborn required extra care and a stay in the neonatal intensive care unit, and she was asked to work the following month on an upcoming product launch. Less than a month after giving birth, she said she was asked to manage an exhibition booth that “required long periods of standing, physical work … and required her to be away from her newborn for approximately 10 hours.” The next month, she said she was asked to work on a video production that was being shot in Brazil. “In its Handbook, ‘How to Succeed In MrBeast Production,’ MrBeast informs employees they are expected to get the job done at any personal cost and no excuse is acceptable,” Mavromatis’ lawsuit said. “She knew if she did not continue to grind and get work done, as asked by MrBeast managers and expected by MrBeast, she would not have a job to return to after her leave.” Mavromatis said she was fired three weeks after returning to work and was told her role was being eliminated. She said a man was later hired to perform duties that she had done as the social media manager. In a statement, Jennifer Mondino, the senior director of the Time’s Up Legal Defense Fund at the National Women’s Law Center, said the allegations reflect a familiar pattern in abusive workplaces. “Abusive workplaces rely on a persistent lack of accountability,” Mondino said in a statement to Newsweek. “We see this pattern frequently, where those with influence and power are allowed to harm others and retaliate against those who decide to speak up.” Mondino praised Mavromatis for coming forward and framed the lawsuit as part of a broader effort to challenge entrenched workplace harassment. “Lorrayne has been extraordinarily brave in coming forward, and we hope she is granted a measure of justice and healing,” Mondino said. “We are in a collective fight to address a long-standing culture of harassment that relies on entrenched silence and shame.” A spokesperson for Beast Industries told Newsweek that Mavromatis’ claims were “clout-chasing allegations.” The spokesperson added that the claims were “built on deliberate misrepresentations and categorically false statements, and we have the receipts to prove it.” The spokesperson continued: “There is extensive evidence—including Slack and WhatsApp messages, company documents, and witness testimony—that unequivocally refutes her claims. We will not submit to opportunistic lawyers looking to manufacture a payday from us.” Related Articles Start your unlimited Newsweek trial NEW YORK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 03: MrBeast, Creator, Entrepreneur and Philanthropist Jimmy Donaldson takes the stage during the 2025 New York Times Dealbook Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center on December 03, 2025 in New York City.
